Translates of a fixed normalized compactly supported function then have Rayleigh quotients tending to minus infinity, contradicting the asserted positive, lower-bounded enumeration. Even V→+∞ alone does not imply positive eigenvalues if negative potential shifts are allowed. The later framework supplies stronger sign assumptions that the opening assertion omits.

The variational formulation needs a finite-potential-energy form domain rather than unrestricted H¹.

issues.failure_explanation: The reported computation is on a polygon containing the disk. A Dirichlet P₁ function on that polygon generally has nonzero trace on the interior circle, so it is not in H₀¹(D(4)). Consequently the asserted intermediate comparison λ_k^R≤λ_{k,h}^{R,P1} does not follow for the reported mesh. Likewise, the computed Neumann eigenvalues belong to the polygon, not the disk. Whole-space bounds can still be justified directly on the polygon.

issues.failure_explanation: The cell-minimum potential error is governed by V's modulus of continuity, for which no power-law bound is assumed. For example, V(x)=|x|²+Σ_{j≥1}2^{-j}(1-cos(2π·2^{2^j}x₁)) is continuous, nonnegative and confining. On aligned meshes of scale h_j≈2^{-2^j}, the high-frequency terms vanish at vertices but have cell averages of order 2^{-j}. The resulting cell-minimum bias, and hence the ground-state bias by a variational test, can decay slower than every power of h_j. The O(h²) Liu correction cannot remove this obstruction.

issues.overall_effect: The unqualified algebraic h-rate is unavailable for the stated class of continuous confining potentials, even if the truncation arguments are repaired.
issues.title: Continuity of the potential does not guarantee algebraic mesh convergence
issues.why_classification: For the advertised continuous-potential class, convergence can be arbitrarily slower than every algebraic rate. A complete repair must either exclude that regime from the rate guarantee or materially weaken the rate.
